cases.sentence: Он с другого же утра стал раздражителен и старательно придирался к брату, затрогивая его за самые ___.
cases.explain: «больные места» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Levin had long before made the observation that when one is uncomfortable with people from their being excessively amenable and meek, one is apt very soon after to find things intolerable from their touchiness and irritability. He felt that this was how it would be with his brother. And his brother Nikolay’s gentleness did in fact not last out for long. The very next morning he began to be irritable, and seemed doing his best to find fault with his brother, attacking him on his tenderest points.

cases.sentence: На ___ Николай вызвал брата высказать опять ему свой план и стал не только осуждать его, но стал умышленно смешивать его с коммунизмом.
cases.explain: «третий день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The third day Nikolay induced his brother to explain his plan to him again, and began not merely attacking it, but intentionally confounding it with communism.

cases.sentence: – А я был и нахожу, что это преждевременно, но разумно и имеет будущность, как христианство в ___.
cases.explain: «первые века» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “But I have, and I consider it’s premature, but rational, and it has a future, just like Christianity in its first ages.”

cases.sentence: – Я только полагаю, что рабочую силу надо рассматривать с ___ зрения, то есть изучить ее, признать ее свойства и…
cases.explain: «естествоиспытательской точки» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “All that I maintain is that the labor force ought to be investigated from the point of view of natural science; that is to say, it ought to be studied, its qualities ascertained. …”

cases.sentence: Везде были рабы, потом metayers; и у нас есть ___, есть аренда, есть батрацкая работа, – чего ты ищешь?
cases.explain: «испольная работа» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But that’s utter waste of time. That force finds a certain form of activity of itself, according to the stage of its development. There have been slaves first everywhere, then métayers; and we have the half-crop system, rent, and day laborers. What are you trying to find?”

cases.sentence: – Ну, ты так думаешь, – и оставь! – отвечал Левин, чувствуя, что мускул ___ его неудержимо прыгает.
cases.explain: «левой щеки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, all right, that’s what you think—and let me alone!” answered Levin, feeling the muscles of his left cheek twitching uncontrollably.

cases.sentence: Встретившись на ___ с Щербацким, двоюродным братом Кити, Левин очень удивил его своею мрачностью.
cases.explain: «железной дороге» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Three days after his brother’s departure, Levin too set off for his foreign tour. Happening to meet Shtcherbatsky, Kitty’s cousin, in the railway train, Levin greatly astonished him by his depression.

cases.sentence: Темнота покрывала для него все; но именно вследствие этой темноты он чувствовал, что единственною руководительною нитью в этой темноте было его дело, и он из ___ ухватился и держался за него.
cases.explain: «последних сил» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Levin said what he had genuinely been thinking of late. He saw nothing but death or the advance towards death in everything. But his cherished scheme only engrossed him the more. Life had to be got through somehow till death did come. Darkness had fallen upon everything for him; but just because of this darkness he felt that the one guiding clue in the darkness was his work, and he clutched it and clung to it with all his strength.
